Container.Name: Unraid-Reverse-Proxy
Container.Overview:
Give every Docker container on your server a friendly name.
Map 192.168.1.50:8080 to openwebui.local, 192.168.1.50:8989 to sonarr.local, and so on. The container runs a reverse proxy that routes by hostname and an mDNS responder that makes those .local names resolve on your LAN — no router, Pi-hole or hosts-file changes needed on any client.
It also serves a launch screen listing every mapped service with a live up/down indicator, plus a password-protected admin panel for managing the routes.
IMPORTANT: assign this container its own IP address on br0 (set Network Type to "Custom: br0" and give it a Fixed IP outside your DHCP pool). The Unraid webGUI already owns port 80 on the host, and the container needs its own IP to use port 80 and to receive mDNS multicast traffic.
Container.Description: Reverse proxy plus mDNS responder that maps your Docker containers to .local hostnames, with a dashboard and admin UI.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Stores config.json — your routes, settings and login.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: Port the proxy and web UI listen on. Leave at 80 when the container has its own br0 IP.

Config.Name: mDNS Port
Config.Description: Multicast DNS. Leave at 5353 — clients will not find .local names on any other port.

Config.Name: HTTP_PORT
Config.Description: Must match the HTTP Port above.
